We need to list files in C drive: maybe "dir C:\". Then create a file: "echo > C:\\testing.txt" or "type nul > C:\\testing.txt". But we should be careful: we might want to create the file in the current directory or C:\? The user didn't specify path. Let's assume they want to create it in C:\. So we can run "type nul > C:\\testing.txt". Or "echo. > C:\\testing.txt". We'll do "type nul > C:\\testing.txt". Also we might want to list files: "dir C:\\". We can combine them into one command: "dir C:\\ && type nul > C:\\testing.txt". But we might want to separate them. The tool expects a single command string. We can pass "dir C:\\ && type nul > C:\\testing.txt". That will list files and then create the file. The unit can be omitted. We'll call the function.

We need to output the result of the command. The tool returns whatever the command outputs. We'll call it.
